title: Native invite signup
lede: The updated iPhone client accepts the emailed invitation, creates the account, and enters native Welcome. This local implementation is not part of the released 1.4 (36) app.

stats.n: Real parser, session safety and URLProtocol request/response contracts.
Cold link, resend/reset, expired-link refresh and provider failures.
No merge, production deployment or App Store upload. Local proof predates the authorized PR push.

changes.h: Inbox proof reaches the guarded route
changes.was: Released 1.4 sends no invite token when registering. PR #620 requires it.
changes.now: The new client validates the canonical HTTPS link, keeps its token in memory, and forwards it through discovery and registration.

changes.h: Existing installs keep a browser path
changes.was: Claiming every emailed setup link as a universal link could also intercept links on installed 1.4 clients.
changes.now: The primary and raw email links use web=1, excluded before the native AASA rule. Native setup is an explicit alternative for the updated app.

verification: 29 Swift unit tests passed; 4 native UI scenarios passed. The refreshed-link warning regression was checked again after the final fix.
Simulator build and unsigned generic iOS release build passed. Web TypeScript, changed-file ESLint and the database-free app build passed.
Native/companion source and email contracts, XcodeGen consistency, documentation verification and diff whitespace checks passed.
Independent client/security review closed the older-client link interception and stale registration error findings.
notes: All API requests in the native scenarios use the existing fixture URL protocol. No account, database, inbox or provider mutation was performed.

Cold-link intake uses the fixture launch URL. Warm delivery uses an explicitly DEBUG-only custom URL bridge into the production HTTPS parser. Apple universal-link association/CDN behavior is not proved by this test.

The shared simulator contained another preview app claiming the same custom scheme. Final warm-link checks used an isolated instance of the same required iPhone model; the original simulator and its apps were preserved.
The earlier keyboard diagnostic captures and source patches are retained separately. Their final scroll offsets were not measured, so they are not presented as a matched visual pair.
Live token delivery, actual shared-backend registration, physical-device association and a future app distribution remain rollout gates. PR #620 is still draft and unmerged.
